clue.text: I am taking some vegetables on a whim

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
pulses are edible seeds such as lentils and peas, so a pulse is some vegetables

explanation.surface: Someone loads up on vegetables on a sudden whim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is a link word: 'on a whim' and 'on impulse' are the same phrase, so 'a whim' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A whim is a sudden urge to act, a synonym for a spontaneous urge.

clue.text: Hero of one party (Liberal)

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A Liberal party member is a hero to many.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is someone worshipped or admired, like a hero.

clue.text: Bird beginning to get out of breath

parts.note: a puffin is a seabird

indicators.note: the beginning of the word get is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bird starts to become breathless.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone panting and gasping hard is winded.

clue.text: Aerobatics giving you wind up

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: to spool thread is to wind it

explanation.surface: Stunt flying gives you the wind up, a British phrase for being scared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind up' looks like the British idiom for fright; 'up' alone is the reversal signal in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Loops are circling manoeuvres flown in stunt displays.

clue.text: Fluctuating income restricts business run for profit

indicators.note: one piece restricting another hems it in, holding it inside
letters that fluctuate shift about, so the word income is rearranged

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: Unstable earnings constrain a company trying to make money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluctuating' gives ENOMIC, and 'restricts' has it hold the company abbreviation; 'run for profit' reads as a verb phrase but describes a venture.
explanation.definitionFit: A venture that pays its way commercially is viable and profitable.

clue.text: Thoroughly out of condition, but comfortable

parts.note: to do something well is to do it thoroughly
food that is off has gone bad, out of condition

explanation.surface: Someone is badly unfit yet perfectly content.
explanation.definitionFit: Being comfortable in the financial sense means having plenty of money, being affluent.

clue.text: Primarily, what all really modern thermals have

definitions.text: Primarily, what all really modern thermals have

indicators.note: primarily, as in at first, points to the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: The latest thermal underwear is chiefly about keeping heat in.
explanation.definitionFit: Heat retention is what thermal underwear exists to give its wearer.

clue.text: Emulsion I used in error for car

indicators.note: letters used in error are put in the wrong order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone used the wrong paint on a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A limousine is a large luxurious chauffeured car.

clue.text: Head's back, turning up in charge within a month

indicators.note: says the turned letters sit inside the month

parts.note: OCT is the abbreviation for October, a month

indicators.note: turning signals that the next words are read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone's head swivels, taking charge within the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' gives CIPU, and 'within' sets that inside the month; 'Head's back' means the back of the head, not a head returning.
explanation.definitionFit: The occiput is the rear of the skull, so the back of the head.

clue.text: Elegant groom's costume

parts.note: fancy means elaborate or elegant
to dress a horse is to groom it; the 's stands for is and gives no letter

explanation.surface: A bridegroom wears a smart outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' is not the bridegroom but the verb, as in dressing a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy-dress outfit is a costume worn to a party in disguise.

clue.text: Not in pink or red?

parts.note: 'in the pink' means in good health, so not in it is unwell; and a person neither pink nor red lacks a colour

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works twice: literally lacking any rosy hue, and idiomatically feeling unwell, the opposite of being in the pink.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling slightly ill is the idiomatic meaning, the reverse of the British idiom 'in the pink' for healthy.

clue.text: Wine bottled in magnum — a Constantia

indicators.note: bottled in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A big bottle holds a South African wine from Constantia.
explanation.definitionFit: Mâcon is a Burgundy wine region and the wine named after it, an example of a wine.

clue.text: Succinctly, and flexibly that's hard to find

parts.note: to say something in short is to say it succinctly
supply as an adverb, from supple, means flexibly

explanation.surface: Something described briefly and nimbly turns out to be rare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' here is not the noun but the adverb of 'supple', pronounced with a short 'ply'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce, with little available, is hard to find.

clue.text: Bearing of Roman who wrote about old agricultural concerns

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: Cato the Elder was a Roman who wrote De Agri Cultura, a treatise on farming
farms are agricultural businesses or concerns

explanation.surface: A Roman author's stance on farming matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' suggests demeanour; in heraldry a bearing is a device on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldic bearings are the emblems displayed on a family shield.

clue.text: Stop working on newspaper, say, producing fine material

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: a newspaper is an example of an organ, a publication speaking for a group
a machine that stops working is said to die

explanation.surface: A paper stopping publication yields a delicate fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Organdie is a sheer, stiff cotton muslin, a kind of delicate fabric.

clue.text: Boring hue spread around border

indicators.note: letters spread around are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A dull colour is splashed around the edging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Border' looks like an edge but is the noun for someone who borders on you.
explanation.definitionFit: A person living next door borders on you, so they adjoin your land.

clue.text: Better qualified mechanic

definitions.meaning: the comparative of fit, more suitable or capable
a tradesman who assembles and repairs machinery

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: more apt for a role, and an engineer who installs machine parts.

clue.text: Capital city that's different, outside one's range of knowledge

indicators.note: says the rearranged letters go round the other piece
different signals that the letters of the word that's are made into something else

parts.note: ken is a range of knowledge, as in beyond one's ken

explanation.surface: A capital that feels unfamiliar lies beyond what one knows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Different' gives TASHT, and 'outside' wraps it round the word for range of knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Tashkent is the capital of Uzbekistan.

clue.text: Warning of poison given verbally

indicators.note: said out loud, so the word for poison is heard rather than written

parts.note: a toxin is a poison

explanation.surface: Someone is warned about poison by word of mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A tocsin is an alarm bell or signal, so a warning.

clue.text: Moderate and constant speed

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, notably the speed of light
to hasten is to speed up

explanation.surface: Driving at a moderate, steady speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate' looks like an adjective but is a verb meaning restrain.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate someone's behaviour is to subdue or restrain them, a verb sense.

clue.text: Starving bird given nothing by us

parts.note: a raven is a bird
O is nought, nothing

explanation.surface: We feed a hungry bird nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone starving is extremely hungry, a close synonym.

clue.text: I'm on sub — unusual form of transport

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters are put into a strange new order

explanation.surface: A sailor boasts about riding an odd vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus is the full name for a bus, public road transport.

clue.text: Arch conforming with others

definitions.meaning: the arched middle of the foot
marching or acting ..., in agreement with everyone else

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the foot's upper arched part, and being in step with the group.

clue.text: Brief success achieved in making flambeed dish

definitions.meaning: an idiom for a sudden success that quickly fizzles out
literally, a burst of flame in the cooking pot when brandy is lit over a dish

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from old flintlock muskets whose powder flared without firing, so a short-lived triumph.

clue.text: Prospects rosy for City here after half-time

definitions.text: Prospects rosy for City here after half-time

parts.words: Prospects rosy for City here after half-time
parts.note: echoes Burgon's poem line 'a rose-red city half as old as time', disguised as a football team winning after the interval

explanation.walkthrough: The football surface hides a famous Victorian poem about the Jordanian rock-cut city.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient Jordanian city carved in pink sandstone is the subject of that poem.

clue.text: Hard wood for ship's wheel

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
elm is a wood

explanation.surface: Tough timber is used to make a ship's wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: The helm is the steering gear of a vessel, its tiller or wheel.

clue.text: Relationship takes a short time in carnival environment

indicators.note: says the earlier pieces are placed inside the carnival city

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is famous as the setting of a great carnival
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A relationship gets a little time at the carnival.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio is a proportional relation between two quantities.

clue.text: Potentially better offer finally accepted by board in afternoon

indicators.note: one piece accepted by another is taken inside it

parts.note: afternoon tea, often just tea, is a light meal taken in the afternoon

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word offer

parts.note: a table is a board, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A deal at an afternoon board meeting could improve things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accepted by' puts R (last of offer) inside TEA to give TREA; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something curable can potentially be made better, the sense here.

clue.text: Hot spot, with United Nations brought in to make secure

indicators.note: says the abbreviation is placed inside the other word

parts.note: to strap something is to fasten it securely

explanation.surface: UN troops are brought in to secure a dangerous hot spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot spot' suggests a conflict zone; here it means a sheltered sunny place.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheltered place that catches the sun, so a warm spot in a garden.

clue.text: Convict finally has to arrange to release bar in window

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word Convict

parts.note: to ransom a captive is to pay to secure their release

explanation.surface: A convict plans an escape through the window bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal crossbar in a window, or above a door.
